title: Platform systems & services — dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki (Q4 2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Platform team’s systems-and-services inventory, standard how-tos, canonical dashboards & alerting rules, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended to be the single source of truth for platform oncall, incident response, and roadmap planning.

Scope
- Systems: control plane (platform-api), metrics pipeline (metrics-collector + prometheus), alert router (alert-router), deployment manager (orch-service), secrets & config (kms-proxy, config-service), and observability (grafana + tempo).
- Audience: oncall engineers, platform owners, SRE, and cross-functional partners (infra, product).

Owners and Contacts
- Platform team leads: Asha Patel (platform systems) — asha.patel@redwood.example.com
- SRE liaison: Marco Rivera — marco.rivera@redwood.example.com
- Pager rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.example.com (see rota in Team Wiki)

Service Inventory (production)
| Service name | Primary owner | Location | SLA / SLO | Criticality |
|--------------|---------------|----------|----------:|------------:|
| platform-api | Platform Core | us-west-2 | 99.95% latency p95 < 150ms | critical |
| metrics-collector | Observability | us-west-2, eu-west-1 | 99.9% scrape availability | high |
| alert-router | Platform Ops | us-west-2 | 99.9% delivery to pager | high |
| orch-service | Deployment Manager | us-west-2 | 99.5% successful deploys | high |
| kms-proxy | Security | private clusters | n/a (compliance) | critical |

Dashboards (canonical)
- Platform Overview (grafana id: 1220) — traffic, request latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, active nodes, queue depth.
- Metrics Pipeline — scrape success rate, ingestion latency, prometheus memory/TSDB size (grafana id: 1304).
- Deployment Health — rollout success %, pending pods, job failures (grafana id: 1401).
- Alerting & Oncall — alert counts by severity, mean time to ack (MTTA), mean time to resolve (MTTR) (grafana id: 1500).

How-tos (common procedures)
1) Add a new Grafana panel (stable pattern):
   - Open dashboard id 1220 -> Edit -> Add panel.
   - Use existing shared variables (env, cluster, service) to avoid panel-level filters.
   - Panel promQL example for platform-api p95:  

     sum by(job) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"platform-api\",env=~\"$env\"}[5m])) by (le)))

   - Save with versioned description: \"Added p95 latency panel — asha 2026-10-12\".

2) Add a Prometheus alert rule (steps):
   - Create alert file under prometheus/rules/platform/ with name service-name-rules.yaml.
   - Rule template (YAML):

     groups:
     - name: platform.rules
       rules:
       - alert: PlatformAPIHighErrorRate
         expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\",code!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\"}[5m])) > 0.02
         for: 5m
         labels:
           severity: page
         annotations:
           summary: \"platform-api error rate > 2% (5m)\"

   - Run make prometheus-lint and CI checks. Submit PR to infra repo; request review from Observability team.

3) Oncall: acknowledge & triage incoming page
   - Acknowledge in Opsgenie. Post initial findings to #platform-oncall (include service, region, p95 latency, error spike).
   - Quick triage checklist:
     1. Check Grafana Platform Overview (id 1220) for traffic pattern changes.
     2. Check Metrics Pipeline dashboard (id 1304) for scrape/backfill issues.
     3. Inspect platform-api pods for OOMs / restarts: kubectl -n platform get pods -o wide --selector=app=platform-api
     4. Check recent deploys: 
        kubectl -n platform rollout history deployment/platform-api || echo \"no rollout events\"
     5. If errors are HTTP 5xx across all instances, consider circuit-breaker or rollback (see Runbook: Service-wide 5xx).

Operational Runbooks (short versions)
- Service-wide 5xx spike (Platform API)
  1. Confirm spike: metrics -> error rate > 2% sustained for 5m.
  2. Check recent config/deploys. If deploy in last 30m, roll back: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/platform-api --to-revision=<previous>.
  3. If OOM/restarts: increase memory request in staging, create hotfix PR, roll out to canary, then to prod.
  4. If external dependency failing (e.g., upstream auth): switch to degraded auth path (feature-flag fallback) and notify upstream team.
  5. Postmortem: create JIRA, tag owner_team:engineering, include timeline and remediation.

- Prometheus / TSDB OOM / high churn
  1. Identify write spikes: check remote_write backlog and ingestion latency.
  2. Scale prometheus-remote or Thanos sidecar horizontally.
  3. If TSDB corrupted, restore from last consistent snapshot (contact Observability owner).

Escalation Matrix
- Severity: page (S0/S1) -> platform oncall -> SRE lead (Marco Rivera) -> Eng director.
- Pager rules: page if severity: page and >3 services affected or platform-api p95 > 300ms for 10m.

Alerting guidelines and thresholds
- Severity mapping: 
  - page: service-wide business impact, immediate action required. Example alerts: PlatformAPIHighErrorRate (>=2% 5m), PlatformAPIHighLatency (p95 > 300ms 10m).
  - ticket: non-blocking degradation. Example: one instance failing healthcheck but load balancer draining works.
  - info: advisory. Example: dashboard panel added or low-priority job failed.
- Example Prometheus alert (High latency):

  alert: PlatformAPIHighLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"platform-api\",env=~\"$env\"}[10m])) by (le)) > 0.3
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: \"platform-api p95 > 300ms for 10m\"

Runbook ownership and SLAs
- Every runbook has a single primary owner and a secondary. Owners are responsible for keeping runbooks updated quarterly.
- Required runbooks (minimum): service-5xx, prometheus-oom, grafana-unavailable, rollout-failure, kms-proxy-failure.
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly during Platform retro.

Retrospectives (last three incidents)
1) Incident: Metrics ingestion lag (2026-05-18) — root cause: remote_write overloaded due to increased client-side cardinality.
   - Actions: enforce scrape config cardinality limits, add client-side relabeling, added synthetic metrics to detect cardinality growth. Owner: Kai Nguyen. Status: complete.
2) Incident: Canary silently failed (2026-07-30) — root cause: rollout job did not block on health checks.
   - Actions: make rollout pipeline require 5 consecutive healthy checks before promoting. Add canary-runbook and a per-service canary-dashboard. Owner: Loretta Chen. Status: in_progress.
3) Incident: platform-api intermittent 503s (2026-09-02) — root cause: downstream auth service rate limiting.
   - Actions: implement exponential backoff, add circuit-breaker and observable counter for auth retries. Owner: Asha Patel. Status: deployed.

Quarterly Roadmap (Q4 2026) — key initiatives
- Observability improvements: reduce alert noise by 40% via consolidated rules and runbook-driven thresholds (owner: Marco Rivera).
- Runbook automation: add automated diagnostics (k8s logs + perf snapshot) for top 5 runbooks (owner: Platform Ops).
- Deployment safety: enforce canary gate in CD and add automated rollback on error-rate regression (owner: Release Engineering).
- Private deployment readiness: harden kms-proxy and config-service for air-gapped installs (owner: Eng Private Deployments).
- Team wiki consolidation: merge service-level playbooks into this canonical doc and add links to per-service pages.

- Service-level runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/*
- Dashboard ownership guide: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-guide

Maintenance and contribution guidelines
- To update this doc, create a PR against confluence-content repo with the updated JSON file and notify reviewers listed above.
- Label new dashboards and alerts with owner and \"reviewed:<YYYY-MM-DD>\" in the description field.
- Quarterly review: each owner must confirm runbook accuracy via a short play (game-day) before the end of each quarter.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Check platform-api pods:
  kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api -o wide
- Rollback last deployment:
  kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/platform-api
- Prometheus query: p95 latency for a service:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"platform-api\"}[5m])) by (le))
- Example alert rule filename: prometheus/rules/platform/platform-api-rules.yaml
